subsystems.name: Quantum processing unit
subsystems.role: the physical qubits whose entangled states stand in for the boundary theory in a holographic duality.
parts: superconducting qubit chip with couplers, or a surface-electrode ion trap

subsystems.name: Control and readout
subsystems.role: prepares states, applies the simulated Hamiltonian and reads out correlations.

subsystems.name: Holographic encoding
subsystems.role: the dictionary that translates a gravity model into a quantum circuit on the boundary.
parts: interaction couplings of toy models such as SYK
circuit compiler that maps couplings to gates

subsystems.name: Error handling
subsystems.role: keeps the simulated state faithful long enough to measure.

subsystems.name: Classical support
subsystems.role: simulates the same model classically to check the quantum results.

subsystems.name: Verification layer
subsystems.role: tests whether the output really behaves like the dual gravity theory.
parts: scrambling diagnostics such as out-of-time-order correlators

buildSteps.title: Pick a tractable dual model
buildSteps.detail: Choose a low-dimensional boundary theory with a known gravity dual, small enough to fit on today's qubits — for example a one-dimensional fermion model with chaotic, all-to-all couplings.

buildSteps.title: Discretise and encode
buildSteps.detail: Put the theory on a lattice, map fermions to qubit operators with a Jordan-Wigner transform, and compile the couplings into a gate sequence using Trotter or variational simulation.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the qubits
buildSteps.detail: For superconducting hardware, pattern aluminium or niobium circuits on a silicon chip with tunable couplers; for ions, mill a surface-electrode trap and load individual atoms.

buildSteps.title: Wire up the environment
buildSteps.detail: Cool the chip to around 10 millikelvin in a dilution refrigerator, or hold ions in ultra-high vacuum with laser cooling; connect signal lines to the control electronics.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate gates
buildSteps.detail: Tune single- and two-qubit gate fidelities with randomised benchmarking until the simulated model's errors are small enough to interpret.

buildSteps.title: Prepare and evolve
buildSteps.detail: Initialise the encoded state, apply the simulated Hamiltonian for a known time, and measure two-point and four-point correlators.

buildSteps.title: Diagnose the gravity signature
buildSteps.detail: Look for the behaviour expected of the dual black hole: fast scrambling, a specific entanglement-entropy pattern, or a negative shockwave response.

buildSteps.title: Cross-check classically
buildSteps.detail: Reproduce the same run with tensor networks or exact diagonalisation for small systems, to confirm the hardware is not simply producing noise.

buildSteps.title: Scale the boundary dimension
buildSteps.detail: Grow qubit count and connectivity until two-dimensional boundary theories, whose dual is three-dimensional gravity, become simulable.

prerequisites.why: it supplies the mathematical translation between a boundary quantum theory and a bulk gravity description.
Trotterisation and variational methods are the algorithms that turn a model into a circuit.
only small logical qubits have been demonstrated; useful simulation of strongly entangled models needs far more.
chaotic dual models need many long-range couplings, which planar superconducting chips serve poorly.

prerequisites.tech: A tested theory of quantum gravity at the Planck scale
prerequisites.why: the Planck energy is about 10^19 GeV, roughly 15 orders of magnitude beyond any accelerator; no experiment currently constrains it.

pathway.milestone: toy holographic models run on a few tens of physical qubits; a 2022 9-qubit superconducting experiment reproduced traversable-wormhole dynamics
pathway.unlocks: proof that holographic models can be expressed as quantum circuits and measured.

pathway.milestone: error-corrected simulation of one- and two-dimensional boundary theories on hundreds of logical qubits
pathway.unlocks: controlled study of scrambling and entanglement structure with credible error bounds.

pathway.milestone: quantum simulators reaching regimes classical tensor networks cannot
pathway.unlocks: a genuine numerical laboratory for quantum-gravity toy models.

pathway.milestone: benchmarking candidate quantum-gravity ideas against simulator output
pathway.unlocks: constraints on holographic proposals — not universe emulation, and not direct access to Planck-scale physics.
